title: OpenAI Launches ChatGPT Ads in India With Over 50 Brands and Self-Serve Access From September
excerpt: India becomes the third major market to get ChatGPT advertising, with WPP and Omnicom as launch partners and a self-serve ads manager opening September 4 for budgets starting at Rs 725 per day.
body:
• OpenAI has launched ChatGPT Ads in India for logged-in adult users on Free and Go plans, with paid tiers remaining ad-free.
  • Over 50 brands will go live this week through agency partners WPP and Omnicom, with self-serve access via ChatGPT Ads Manager opening September 4.
  • Daily campaign budgets start at Rs 725, opening the platform to small and medium businesses alongside large advertisers.
  • India is the third major region after the US and Europe to get ChatGPT advertising, as OpenAI pursues revenue diversification ahead of its public listing.

OpenAI has rolled out advertising on ChatGPT in India, making it the third major market — after the United States and Europe — to see sponsored content within the AI chatbot's conversational interface.

The launch, announced on August 27, will show ads to logged-in adults using ChatGPT's Free and Go tiers. Paid subscriptions including Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise, and Education will remain ad-free. More than 50 brands are expected to begin advertising on the platform this week.

How ChatGPT Ads Work

Ads will appear below ChatGPT's organic response when a user's query shows commercial intent and a relevant sponsored product or service is available. The ads will be clearly labelled as sponsored and displayed independently from the AI-generated answer.

OpenAI has emphasised that advertisements will not influence ChatGPT's responses or alter how the system prioritises user needs. Advertisers will not receive access to users' conversation text, chat history, memories, or personal information. Instead, they will get conventional aggregate campaign metrics — impressions, clicks, click-through rates, conversions, and return on investment.

The company said ads will not be shown to users identified or predicted to be under 18, and will not appear alongside sensitive or regulated topics including mental health and politics. OpenAI expects ads to appear in roughly one out of five queries for eligible Indian users, primarily during conversations with commercial intent.

India as a Key Market

"India is one of the most dynamic markets in the world for how people use ChatGPT to learn, build, and discover. Our weekly active users have doubled year-on-year."

— Dave Dugan, VP and Head of Global Ads Solutions, OpenAI

WPP and Omnicom will serve as OpenAI's first agency partners for ChatGPT Ads in India, a non-exclusive arrangement. From September 4, businesses of all sizes will be able to access a self-serve ChatGPT Ads Manager with daily campaign budgets starting as low as Rs 725 — a move designed to open the platform beyond large brands to India's extensive network of small and medium enterprises.

OpenAI said it expects early advertiser interest across travel, financial services, retail, and health and beauty sectors. The company described India's opportunity as a combination of large enterprises, a sophisticated agency ecosystem, and a long tail of SMBs that can use self-serve tools.

A Different Ad Model

OpenAI is positioning ChatGPT advertising as fundamentally different from conventional search ads. Rather than relying on keyword bidding or long-term advertising profiles, relevance is determined by the immediate intent expressed during a conversation. The company frames this as reaching users at "high-context moments when decisions are beginning to take shape."

Users will be able to dismiss ads, provide feedback on why they were shown a particular ad, and turn off personalisation or clear ad-related data at any time. OpenAI also plans to support action-based buying models, conversion tools, and integration with independent measurement partners.

Revenue Diversification Before IPO

The India advertising launch comes as OpenAI prepares for its public listing later this year. The company has been diversifying revenue streams beyond its subscription business, and India — one of ChatGPT's largest and most active markets by user count — represents a significant advertising opportunity. The move signals how aggressively OpenAI is pursuing ad revenue while maintaining the ad-free experience for paying subscribers.
nri_angle: Indian tech professionals and entrepreneurs in the diaspora who use ChatGPT daily will see ads on free tiers, while the self-serve platform creates a new channel for India-based businesses targeting NRI consumers.
